newsitem.title: USA: Miami oversight board rejects budget plan.
newsitem.headline: Miami oversight board rejects budget plan.

text.p: A state-appointed oversight board rejected Miami's deficit bailout plan on Tuesday, saying some of the city's revenue estimates were doubtful.
Lt. Gov. Buddy MacKay, who chairs the oversight board, said $9.9 million of the revenues in the city's $68 million bailout plan were "too iffy" to consider as solid revenues.
Those included $2.2 million in federal grants to police that the city has yet to receive and $3.1 million of overdue garbage collection fees Miami hopes to recover through liens.
The board also said that the city needs to add $13.6 million, or 20 percent of its $68 million annual budget deficit, in financial reserves against uncollected funds or emergencies.

Board members said the 20-percent cushion was crucial because the city still does not know exactly how big its deficit is. The $68 million figure for fiscal 1997 is based on an estimated carrry-over deficit of $19 million from fiscal 1996, which ended September 30 and is still under audit.
"We haven't really verified that number," board member Cynthia Curry said.
The board's only option was to accept or reject the entire plan. However, board members said that at least 85 percent of the plan seemed acceptable.
"I think we are close," board member Robert Beatty said.

City Manager Ed Marquez said the city may be able to meet the board's request for $23.5 million of new revenues through land sales and leases, including lease revenues from waterfront property earmarked for a new basketball arena.
"I think we will be albe to come back to them with a plan that will be acceptable," Marquez said.
Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles appointed the board to guide Miami's fiscal recovery last month.

Miami has spent more money than it took in for years. But the $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget for the year that began October 1 only came to light after three top city officials resigned to face federal corruption charges.
